claims.exact_statement: For every nonconstant f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1} with relevant support R and every cover of R by M>=1 ordered subsets R_t (ranks r_t, strict predecessor sets U_j^t): H(f) <= h2(Var f) + (K_ref + log2 M) I(f) + (6/(5 ln 2)) sum_A fhat(A)^2 sum_{j in A} min_{t: j in R_t} ln( r_t(j)/(|A cap U_j^t|+1) ), K_ref = 3+2log2(3)+log2(6e).
hypotheses: ordered cover of the relevant support

claims.exact_statement: For one order (M=1) the rank term equals sum_j Inf_j(f) ln r(j) - E_{P_f} ln|A|!, minimized by ordering coordinates by decreasing influence; hence H(f) <= h2(Var f) + K_ref I(f) + (6/(5 ln 2))[sum_i Inf_(i) ln i - E_{P_f} ln|A|!].

For tribes T_{m,w} (OR of m disjoint ANDs of width w, q=1-2^-w) and every single-gate table (any M, any ordered M-cover), the right side of L1 is >= h2(v) + K_ref I + (1 - (6/5) q^{m-1}) I log2 M + (6/5) q^{m-1} I log2(m/e). At m=2^w the ratio to I tends to infinity (about K_ref + 0.44(w-1.44)) while H/I tends to 4, so no single-gate table certifies FEI with an absolute constant; the one-gate-per-block forest has bound/I <= 13.40 in the limit (13.34 at w=60).
hypotheses: divergence statement taken at m=2^w, where q^(m-1)=(1-1/m)^(m-1)<=1/2 makes the M term nonnegative; the displayed inequality holds for every m,w and M
